output:
**Not under the current rules.** The rules file lists `is.waiwai.dictation` as a permanent release invariant, because existing Accessibility permission grants depend on it. A rename means deliberately revoking that invariant, which is your call as owner, and I wouldn't do it as a routine change.

If you do want it, before launch is the cheapest time, since the cost grows with every install. The rename would have these effects:

- **Accessibility grants:** macOS ties these to the bundle identifier, so every existing install (beta testers, your own machines) would see the renamed app as a new app and have to re-grant Accessibility. The old entry stays behind in System Settings.
- **Other permissions:** the same applies to any other macOS permission the app holds, such as Microphone.
- **Preferences:** the defaults domain is keyed on the bundle ID, so saved settings would be lost unless you write a migration. Any data stored under a bundle-ID-named path would be orphaned the same way.
- **Updates:** I can't check from here whether existing builds would update cleanly to a renamed app through Sparkle. Test that before relying on it. The EdDSA key must stay the same either way.

**Recommendation:** keep `is.waiwai.dictation`. Users almost never see the bundle identifier, so you can brand the app OpenRamble through its display name, app name and marketing at no cost.

The rename is only worth it if the installed base is small enough to tell everyone personally to re-grant permissions. In that case, do it once before launch and update the rules file to make the new identifier the permanent one.

How many installs exist outside your own machines? That decides how expensive this is.
